Header:
Date: 2027-03-11
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (HelioCloud Partnerships), Diego Ramirez (HelioCloud Platform), Liu Wei (HelioCloud Security)

Topics: Marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture, packaging (Helm/chart), security/GDPR/SOC2, billing/entitlements, compatibility testing plan

[00:00] Alex Carter: okay hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll give it a minute for folks to pop in i'm alex carter from Redwood, i'm the AE on this engagement, with me is priya singh, our solutions engineer.
[00:15] Priya Singh: hi all, thanks, yeah excited to sync, we put together a rough ref arch and some questions for the marketplace listing.
[00:30] Maya Patel: hey hi thanks for the invite, maya here, quick agenda note — procurement and listing timeline is our priority, but platform compatibility is close second.
[00:45] Diego Ramirez: morning, diego, i've got a few notes on our k8s environment and storage that i want to run by you.
[01:05] Alex Carter: great, let's run through the marketplace checklist first — i want to understand helio's listing requirements, metadata, billing hooks, procurement flows. maya can you outline the must-haves?
[01:20] Maya Patel: sure, so for helio we need: 1) marketplace tile with logos and short summary, 2) deployment options (managed on helio vs bring-your-own), 3) entitlements and meter integration for usage billing, 4) security badge info (SOC2/ISO), and 5) a reference architecture doc ideally with deploy scripts or helm charts. we'll also need the vendor support contact and an approved logo.
[01:40] Priya Singh: okay that matches what we typically provide; for entitlements we can support both subscription SKUs and per-token usage metering via billing webhook. examples: monthly reserved capacity SKU and a pay-as-you-go meter.
[01:55] Liu Wei: when you say per-token, how do you handle PII and encryption in transit? we need KMS integration plus audit logs so we can satisfy our compliance.
[02:10] Priya Singh: yes, we have KMS/HSM integrations — customer-managed keys are supported for private deployments; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. the wording in the marketplace listing may need to say "customer-managed keys with KMS integration" — sometimes the auto transcript from our docs says K-V cash instead of KV cache so watch the text.
[02:35] Diego Ramirez: haha, KV cash, yep, we've seen that. on our side we're running k8s 1.27 with nginx ingress, rbd storage for persistent volumes, and we've got an internal VPC setup. we want to know the recommended reference arch for dedicated vs private deployment.
[02:55] Priya Singh: okay for private deployments (on HelioCloud) we recommend a control-plane in helio VPC with a customer-managed data plane — but we can also provide a fully managed option. reference arch will include network diagrams, subnetting recommendations, egress rules, and IAM roles. we'll produce a diagram that maps to your VPC model.
[03:15] Alex Carter: also want to call out autoscaling / GPU pools — if you're offering marketplace-managed instances we'll detail the dedicated GPU pool integration and autoscale policy suggestions. what's your target latency SLA for 99th percentile?
[03:30] Diego Ramirez: primary use case is < 150 ms p99 for short chat interactions; batch embeddings can be slower. cost is a factor so we might put lower tier routes on cheaper instances, fallback to higher perf models.
[03:45] Priya Singh: that's inline with typical profiles — we'll suggest a model routing policy and quantization guidance for embeddings vs chat.
[03:55] Maya Patel: i want to understand packaging. do you provide helm charts or a marketplace terraform module? our marketplace prefers a helm-based install for our managed offering plus an operator for upgrades.
[04:15] Priya Singh: yes we can provide helm charts and a reference operator pattern. we'll include a sample values.yaml for both managed and BYO modes. the chart will expose healthz, metrics endpoints, and a sidecar for log forwarding.
[04:35] Alex Carter: can you also include a quickstart on the listing — like one-click deploy guidances? some customers expect an "install on my cluster" flow.
[04:50] Maya Patel: yes, our marketplace supports an external installer link and also a managed deployment flow. for billing we'll need meter integration details, and for managed we'll need support-level entitlements.
[05:05] Priya Singh: we'll add a table of entitlements — what is included at each tier (SLA, retention, token quota).
[05:20] Liu Wei: security — we require SOC 2 type II evidence and a list of controls, SSO with SAML, RBAC mapping, and encryption at rest with KMS. do you provide whitepapers or audit artifacts?
[05:35] Alex Carter: yes, we have SOC 2 documentation and can provide an SOC 2 report under NDA; we also support SAML SSO and OIDC, plus role-based access control. we'll call out audit log export options for your compliance team.
[05:55] Diego Ramirez: also curious on network egress and data residency — some tenants will need data to remain in the customer VPC. what's your recommended pattern?
[06:10] Priya Singh: for customer data residency we support private deployment where all data stays in your VPC and keys are customer-managed. for hosted deployments we offer region pinning; but for high compliance customers we recommend the private deployment bundle.
[06:30] Maya Patel: on the listing page we often surface whether an offering supports private deployments and whether keys can be customer-managed — can you confirm exact phrasing?
[06:45] Priya Singh: suggest wording: "Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) supported; customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; SOC 2 Type II available under NDA." we can iterate on copy with your marketing folks.
[07:05] Alex Carter: good. technical deep-dive — diego, can you share a few more details about your staging cluster and CI pipeline so priya can prepare a compatibility check?
[07:20] Diego Ramirez: we use gitops with flux, pipelines trigger helm upgrades; we can provide a staging kubeconfig with limited rights. storage uses rbd and we rely on NFS for some workloads. we also have an internal ingress with JWT auth.
[07:40] Priya Singh: that helps — we'll prepare a compatibility test plan focusing on ingress, persistent volumes, and sidecar logging. also check our recommended kernel settings for nvidia drivers if you're planning GPU instances.
[08:00] Maya Patel: timeline — marketplace listing needs vendor materials by 2027-03-25 for our April storefront refresh. is that feasible?
[08:15] Alex Carter: yes, we can hit that if we get the reference arch and the entitlements doc this week and the helm artifacts next week.
[08:30] Diego Ramirez: one small note on operator upgrades — we need a canary upgrade approach. does your operator support canary rollouts?
[08:45] Priya Singh: yes, our operator supports canary releases via annotations and also integrates with standard canary tooling (e.g., flagger). we'll document the rollout policy.
[09:05] Alex Carter: let's cover entitlements mapping — for marketplace we need SKU IDs, human-readable names, metric hooks and meter dimensions. priya, how do you usually expose meter hooks?
[09:20] Priya Singh: we expose a billing webhook that emits usage events and a metering endpoint that can be polled by marketplace platforms. we'll provide a sample payload and test harness.
[09:40] Liu Wei: on security again — will events contain PII? if so we need stripping configs and hashing.
[09:55] Priya Singh: events do not contain raw PII by default; we can add a data-sanitization layer and provide masking config. we'll include that in the ref arch.
[10:20] Maya Patel: procurement side — for managed offering, we require an escalation contact and a 24/7 pager for P1s. is that something you provide?
[10:35] Alex Carter: for enterprise managed customers we have SLA-backed support tiers with on-call rotations; we'll include support contacts in the listing metadata.
[10:55] Diego Ramirez: one more technical: KV cache memory utilization — we need to understand how the cache scales across GPUs and if there are cross-node cache warmups.
[11:10] Priya Singh: good question — our runtime uses shardable KV cache per-instance and supports a warmup strategy with prefix caching. there are tradeoffs between latency and memory; we'll include recommended configs for your expected seq lengths. apologies if i say KV cash earlier — transcription weirdness.
[11:35] Alex Carter: lol. ok, next, packaging artifacts. priya, can you outline deliverables you plan to share?
[11:50] Priya Singh: sure — deliverables: 1) reference architecture diagram (png + drawio), 2) helm chart and values.yaml examples, 3) operator notes for canary upgrades, 4) billing webhook spec and sample payloads, 5) security checklist (SOC2, SAML, KMS, audit logs), 6) quickstart guide for marketplace tile.
[12:15] Diego Ramirez: that looks good. for helm chart we'll need imagePullSecrets and ability to override resource requests so we can test on smaller nodes in staging.
[12:30] Priya Singh: yep we'll parameterize that.
[12:40] Maya Patel: marketing copy — we'll want a one-paragraph description, key features bullets, and a short screenshot of the console. can you provide that?
[12:55] Alex Carter: yes we'll put together a short paragraph and two screenshots — console, and the deploy flow.
[13:15] Liu Wei: regarding audit artifacts — we will want a SOC2 artifact but also a data-flow diagram for our auditors. can that be included?
[13:30] Priya Singh: absolutely, we'll include a dataflow diagram with annotations of what is encrypted and where keys are stored.
[13:45] Maya Patel: last item — GTM: we prefer a co-marketing blurb and then a joint webinar after listing. is redwood open to that?
[14:00] Alex Carter: yes, we're open to joint webinars and a reference case; we'll coordinate with your marketing to schedule after listing goes live.
[14:15] Diego Ramirez: logistics: i'll provision staging access and a test namespace; look for an email from me with kubeconfig and CI pipeline notes.
[14:30] Priya Singh: great, we'll use that for a quick smoke test — ingress, PV, and a token-batched inference call.
[14:45] Alex Carter: recap: priya will draft ref arch by 3/18, alex will share pricing SKUs by 3/15, maya will send marketplace metadata by 3/16, diego will provide staging access by 3/20, liu will provide security requirements by 3/17. everyone ok?
[15:05] Maya Patel: yep that's good.
[15:15] Liu Wei: sounds good.
[15:25] Priya Singh: thanks all, we'll follow up with a doc and a confluence page link.
[15:35] Alex Carter: thanks everyone — we'll send meeting notes and action items. bye.
